sources.note: Shows that reasoning ability can be incentivized in an LLM by pure reinforcement learning on verifiable tasks, with no human-annotated reasoning trajectories, and that the resulting reasoning patterns can be transferred to smaller models.
sources.title: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via Reinforcement Learning

sources.note: Has a teacher decompose and prune a student's reasoning by mathematical skill, then distills the pruned paths back, on the argument that CoT structure must match student capacity.
sources.title: DRP: Distilled Reasoning Pruning with Mathematical Skill-aware Step Decomposition for Efficient Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: A 4B small reasoning model that classifies document-claim pairs as grounded or hallucinated for RAG pipelines and produces evidence-grounded justifications.
sources.title: HalluGuard: Evidence-Grounded Small Reasoning Models to Mitigate Hallucinations in Retrieval-Augmented Generation

sources.note: Finds that the </think> token aggregates the reasoning chain in deep layers and that attention paid to it from that position ranks which steps matter, then uses that ranking to drive a four-operator compression search — cutting 58% of tokens with accuracy holding.
sources.title: CRISP: Compressing Redundancy in Chain-of-Thought via Intrinsic Saliency Pruning

sources.note: Runs the head-to-head this literature had been missing, comparing three importance criteria on the same traces at matched compression ratios, and finds step-level criteria agree on what to keep while disagreeing on what to cut — because redundancy is diffuse rather than located in any identifiable class of step.
sources.title: When Compression Helps and When It Hurts: Condition-Aware Analysis of Chain-of-Thought Distillation

sources.note: Measures RLVR-trained models against their base models with pass@k at large k and finds the base wins, concluding RLVR sharpens sampling toward paths the base already had rather than adding new ones.
sources.title: Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity in LLMs Beyond the Base Model?

sources.note: Reads a reasoning trajectory as a multi-step pseudo-gradient descent on the model's own parameters, which makes each token an optimization step, the trajectory an inner loop, and the training regime a meta-learning problem in which the question is the task.
sources.title: Deciphering Trajectory-Aided LLM Reasoning: An Optimization Perspective

result.definition: Training a smaller model on long reasoning traces from a larger one, and across 7 sources both a widely used capability transfer and the comparison that complicates the archive's reinforcement-learning results. Two findings. It does transfer capability where on-policy methods do not: evaluated identically across sampling budgets, off-policy distillation is higher on both coverage and average correctness at every budget while on-policy distillation's advantage reverses at large budgets. And it is the right control for several claims: one exploration study's controlled comparison is verifiable-reward training against long-chain distillation from the same base rather than against the base model, so 'reduces exploration' there means relative to a distilled policy trained on the same data. The corpus's caution is about attribution -- one source's strongest supervised arm learns from a 14B distilled reasoning model while its reinforcement arm has no teacher at all, so a headline supervised-versus-reinforcement comparison confounds the trace source with the training method. Several archived efficiency methods distil pruned or compressed traces rather than raw ones, and one head-to-head finds step-level importance criteria agreeing on what to keep while disagreeing on what to cut, because redundancy is diffuse rather than located in an identifiable class of step.
